claim_verdicts.evidence: Reproduced: HS256 token signed with .env JWT_SIGNING_KEY, iss donhang-api, aud donhang-app, exp = now-600 s -> 401, Www-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="The token expired at '09/25/2026 02:08:28'".

OrdersController.cs @ stage-1 49-56: [Authorize] [HttpGet] public async Task<ActionResult<List<OrderSummaryDto>>> List() { var customerId = int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub)!); ... }. Class route "api/v1/orders" (line 11) -> List answers GET /api/v1/orders. Block matches source verbatim.

RFC 9110 15.5.2: 401 "lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource". 15.5.4: "If authentication credentials were provided in the request, the server considers them insufficient to grant access. The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials." ASP.NET Core: "forbid action is called by Authorization when an authenticated user attempts to access a resource they're not permitted to access." Lesson now says "the same caller's token".

RFC 9110 15.5.2: "The server generating a 401 response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field ... containing at least one challenge". RFC 6750 s.3 (round 1 WebFetch): resource server SHOULD include error when a token was sent and failed; invalid_token covers expired/malformed. Live: no token -> Bearer; bad token -> Bearer error="invalid_token".

TokenValidationParameters.DefaultClockSkew: "Default for the clock skew." Remarks: "300 seconds (5 minutes)." Program.cs sets no ClockSkew. Live, key-signed tokens: exp now-60 s -> 200, now-290 s -> 200, now-310 s -> 401 "The token expired at ...", now-600 s -> 401.

ValidateIssuerSigningKey: "controls if validation of the SecurityKey that signed the securityToken is called." Remarks: "The default is false." Live: token signed with a different key -> 401 error_description="The signature key was not found"; token signed with the .env key -> 200. Signature check uses IssuerSigningKey; "only tokens signed with that key can pass" holds.
RFC 9110 5.1: "Field names are case-insensitive". Live curl -i output prints "Www-Authenticate:".

authentication/index.md: "The AddAuthentication parameter JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme is the name of the scheme to use by default when a specific scheme isn't requested." Scheme-specific methods "such as AddJwtBearer ... register schemes with appropriate settings." "Calling UseAuthentication registers the middleware that uses the previously registered authentication schemes."

issues.fix: Add a claims entry: kind behavior, version_key aspnetcore, section 4, text "The JWT bearer handler reads the token from the Authorization header after 'Bearer '", source_hint refs/aspnetcore-docs/aspnetcore/security/authentication/configure-jwt-bearer-authentication.md line 16 + live curl. issues.text: The observable symptom does not follow from the misconception. The misconception is answering 403 for a missing/invalid token; the sentence instead describes an API answering 403 correctly, for an identified caller, and says the client "stops working" - a client that re-logs only on 401 behaves correctly there. Quiz q4 has the right symptom.
issues.quote: You notice this when a client that treats every `401` as "log in again" stops working the moment an endpoint answers `403` for a caller it has already identified.
issues.fix: Replace with: "You notice this when an API answers `403` for an expired token: a client that sends the user to log in only on `401` never does, and every call keeps failing."

issues.text: Generalises a property of this app to all endpoints. An action without its own [Authorize] is still protected under a class-level [Authorize] or an authorization fallback policy; it runs here only because OrdersController has neither and AddAuthorization() sets no fallback (Program.cs:43). Same over-reach in quiz q1 explanation d: "an unmarked endpoint is never rejected".
issues.quote: An endpoint without `[Authorize]` runs whatever token is sent, valid or not.
issues.fix: Summary line 3: "In Đơn Hàng, an endpoint without `[Authorize]` runs whatever token is sent, valid or not." q1 explanation d (en): replace "and in any case an unmarked endpoint is never rejected" with "and in Đơn Hàng an unmarked endpoint is not rejected"; vi: "và trong Đơn Hàng endpoint không đánh dấu không bị từ chối".

issues.text: `WWW-Authenticate` is never explained. I know what a header is, but not that this one is where a 401 tells the client why it was refused. Sections 2, 4, 6 and 7 all lean on it (`error="invalid_token"`, `error_description`), so I can match the strings but not say what the header is for.
issues.quote: but the response now carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`
issues.fix: Add one sentence in Core concepts (or on the 401 line): "A `401` always comes with a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming how to authenticate (`Bearer`) and, when a token was sent but rejected, why (`error=...`)."

issues.text: "Bearer" / the `Authorization: Bearer` header is not in my vocabulary and the prereq summaries never say how a client sends the JWT back to the API. I guess the token goes after the word Bearer in that header, but the lesson never states it, and it is the input `UseAuthentication` reads.
issues.quote: the middleware that reads the `Authorization: Bearer` header
issues.fix: Add one sentence to Core concepts: "A client sends its JWT in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`; 'Bearer' just means 'whoever holds this token'."

issues.text: Section 4 says a missing header and a bad token both end the same way: "the request simply carries no caller". Yet the 401s differ: only the bad token gets `error="invalid_token"`, and an expired one gets `error_description`. If `UseAuthorization` only sees "no caller", how does it know why? I cannot reconstruct that step.
issues.quote: If the header is missing or the token fails any check, the request simply carries no caller. Nothing is rejected yet.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after "Nothing is rejected yet." saying that `UseAuthentication` also remembers why the token failed, and that this reason is what ends up in the `WWW-Authenticate` header once `UseAuthorization` answers `401`.

issues.text: The prose says the block configures `UseAuthentication`, but the block only has `AddAuthentication` and `AddJwtBearer`; neither `UseAuthentication` nor `UseAuthorization` appears in any block. From the middleware prereq I expect to see `app.Use...` calls in order, and I cannot tell how `AddJwtBearer` settings reach `UseAuthentication`.
issues.quote: `Program.cs` tells `UseAuthentication` what a valid token looks like:
issues.fix: Add one sentence after the block: "`AddAuthentication`/`AddJwtBearer` only register these rules; `app.UseAuthentication()` and then `app.UseAuthorization()`, further down `Program.cs`, put the two middleware in the pipeline that apply them."

issues.text: `JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme` (an "authentication scheme") appears in the code with no word in the prose. I don't know what a scheme is or whether it matters for the lesson.
issues.quote: builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
issues.fix: Add one clause to the sentence after the block: "`JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme` just says 'check callers by their Bearer JWT'."

issues.text: The comment and `options.MapInboundClaims = false` mention `ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier` URI and "maps them by default" — unknown to me, and the prose never says whether to care. Quiz q5 then uses this line as an option.
issues.quote: options.MapInboundClaims = false;
issues.fix: Add one sentence: "The `MapInboundClaims` line only keeps claim names such as `sub` exactly as issued, so `List` can read `sub`; it does not accept or reject anything."

issues.text: `User` in `List` is never tied to "records who the caller is" from Core concepts. I infer `User` is that recorded caller, but the lesson does not say so.
issues.quote: so reading `sub` from `User` is safe
issues.fix: Change to: "so reading `sub` from `User` — the caller `UseAuthentication` recorded — is safe."

issues.text: Section 4 says issuer/audience must be `donhang-api`/`donhang-app`, but the code reads `Configuration["Jwt:Issuer"]` and `["Jwt:Audience"]`. The prose does not link the two, and `ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true` is the only Validate line the prose skips, so I don't know what it does.
issues.quote: `ValidateIssuer`, `ValidateAudience` and `ValidateLifetime` name the issuer, audience and `exp` checks.
issues.fix: Add "(configured as `donhang-api` and `donhang-app` under `Jwt:Issuer` and `Jwt:Audience`)" after "audience" in that sentence.

issues.text: The whole surprise rests on `Get` lacking `[Authorize]`, but `Get` is not shown and nothing says `List` answers `GET /api/v1/orders` and `Get` answers `GET /api/v1/orders/1`. I take it on trust.
issues.quote: `Get`, a few lines above it in the same file, has no `[Authorize]`
issues.fix: Add "(the action behind `GET /api/v1/orders/{id}`)" after `Get`, and "(behind `GET /api/v1/orders`)" where `List` is first named.

issues.text: The diagram names `UseAuthentication` but not `UseAuthorization`, though the prose says the rejecting happens there. I had to guess that the two diamonds are `UseAuthorization`.
issues.quote: The rejecting happens one step later, in `UseAuthorization`
issues.fix: Label the first diamond "UseAuthorization: endpoint has Authorize?" so the prose's second step has a node.

issues.text: The first paragraph of section 4 packs signature, issuer, audience, exp, leeway and the outcome into one long sentence; I re-read it twice to find where the check ends.
issues.quote: the signature has to match what the signing key produces, the issuer and audience have to be `donhang-api` and `donhang-app`, and `exp` must not have passed — the check allows a few minutes of leeway
issues.fix: Split after "must not have passed." and make the leeway its own sentence: "The check allows a few minutes of leeway for clock differences, so a token just past `exp` can still pass."

issues.text: The 401/403 "you notice this" sentence confused me: why would a client that re-logs on 401 "stop working" on 403? I had to re-read it; the concrete failure (user stuck, or looping) is not named.
issues.quote: You notice this when a client that treats every `401` as "log in again" stops working the moment an endpoint answers `403` for a caller it has already identified.
issues.fix: Name the concrete symptom, e.g. "You notice this when an API answers `403` for an expired token: the app, which only re-logs on `401`, never sends the user to log in and every call keeps failing."

issues.text: Seeing `WWW-Authenticate` depends on `-i` printing response headers, which is not said. Also, section 2 says the made-up token's response "now carries" the header, implying the no-token 401 had none, but Expected result says step 1 has `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
issues.quote: call `curl -s -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders` with no token.
issues.fix: Add "(`-i` prints the response headers)" to step 1, and in section 2 write "it is `401` again, but the header now reads `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error=\"invalid_token\"`".

issues.text: The correct option reuses the lesson's sentence "the request simply carries no caller" almost verbatim, so it can be picked by recognition.
issues.quote: The endpoint runs; the token failed its checks, so the request simply carries no caller
issues.fix: Reword option a, e.g. "The endpoint runs, and it has no identified caller".

issues.text: Option c is clearly the longest and echoes the misconception's correction ("a token well past it is rejected"), so it is guessable without understanding.
issues.quote: False, because expiry is checked on its own, apart from the signature, and a token well past `exp` is rejected.
issues.fix: Shorten c to "False: expiry is a separate check from the signature" and lengthen a distractor (e.g. d) to similar size.

issues.text: Explanation d uses `aud`, which the lesson never shows (it says "audience"). Explanation b says the line "validates the signing key itself", but the lesson never says what that means versus the signature check, so it leaves me more unsure.
issues.quote: This checks that `aud` is `donhang-app`, not when the token expires.
issues.fix: In d write "the audience" instead of `aud`; in b say "The lesson's signature check uses `IssuerSigningKey`; this line is not about `exp`."
